notes: Sweep 2026-10-31-b at head 74112b4 (uncommitted false in every result.json): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier, and every assistant message in each transcript comes from that model. No transcript has a Skill tool call or any SKILL.md text, and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line ("Do not invoke any skills.") requires. All five added tests. skills_listed is 209 in every result.json, as in 2026-10-31. Tool calls are numbered once per tool_use id, counting every tool (Bash, Read, Write, Edit), as in earlier grades.

Rules changed since 0814e8d (git diff 0814e8d -- idiomatic-elixir/): none of this case's seven rules. SKILL.md changed only under One expression per line, and tabular clauses and Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else, both about `for`; macros.md and processes.md also changed. No run writes a `for`, a macro or a process, so those changes touch no verdict and no other_violations entry. All seven rules are graded to the 2026-10-31 standard.

Update structs (unchanged): the defstruct sentence decides. opus-1 writes defstruct [:items, :discount] (line 9) and is clean; haiku-1 (line 7) and haiku-2 (line 9) write defstruct [:items, discount_code: nil], sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 (line 9) defstruct [:items, discount: nil]. 4 of 5 violated, the same split as 2026-10-31. All five follow the update-syntax sentences; Map.put/3 or Map.delete/2 on the inner items map inside %{cart | items: ...} is not the forbidden pattern, as before.

Chain fallible steps with `with` (unchanged): 0 of 5 violated (2026-10-31: 0 of 5). Three runs write one-step with blocks with no else and a body that cannot fail: opus-1 apply_code/2 (lines 52-54), sonnet-1 apply_code/2 (lines 65-67) and total_price/2 (lines 82-84), sonnet-2 total_price/2 (lines 83-85): clean. haiku-2 (lines 57-60) and sonnet-2 (lines 64-67) write case on parse code functions that return :error, mapping it to {:error, :unknown_code}; that is not a pass-through, so it is the case the rule asks for. haiku-2 writes no with and has no other fallible call, and I grade it clean rather than not exercised because the 2026-10-31 grades say the old standard (a case for a single fallible call is not exercised) no longer applies, so the Haiku tier moves from not exercised to clean. Holding that case to not exercised would put the tier back at not exercised and change no violation count. haiku-1 checks membership with if: not exercised. No run writes a pass-through case, an else or a nested fallible case.

Before you finish (unchanged): step 1 is met by a project-wide mix format or a passing mix format --check-formatted after the last edit; a mix test that compiles the app with no warnings stands in for step 2; step 3 (mix credo --strict) is required since the project has Credo. opus-1 (#10) and haiku-2 (#8, #10-#12) did all of it after their last edits and are clean. haiku-1 (#9 test, #10 check), sonnet-1 (#8) and sonnet-2 (#8) never ran Credo and break step 3. 3 of 5 violated (2026-10-31: 4 of 5); haiku-2 is the run that changed. Per tier the split is the same as 2026-10-31: opus clean, Haiku and Sonnet violated.

Per-file formatting check line: missed in 5 of 5, as in 2026-10-31. Every run wrote lib/shop/cart.ex and then edited test/shop/cart_test.exs before any format or check, and formatted or checked once, project-wide: opus-1 and the Sonnet runs in the same command as the tests, the Haiku runs after the tests had run. Replay: every successful Write and Edit applied in order to the case's shop-project files gives files byte-identical to each run's final files, so the formatter changed nothing in any run.

Refused commands: opus-1 none; haiku-1 #1 (find -exec), #2 (cd before git status) and #8 (mix test and a format check chained with echo); haiku-2 #1 (xargs sh -c) and #9 (format check, compile and credo --strict chained with echo); sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 #1 (xargs ls chains) and #5 (python3 heredoc edits chained with mix format && mix test). Each was re-run as plain commands or replaced by Read, Write and Edit. Only haiku-2 #9 carried mix credo --strict, and it was re-run as #12, so no refusal changes a Before you finish verdict.

Other unchanged rules, graded to the 2026-10-31 standard. Return tuples: opus-1 (line 74), haiku-1 (line 78) and haiku-2 (line 79) raise KeyError on an unpriced SKU and say so in the @doc, counted clean; both Sonnet runs return {:error, {:unknown_sku, sku}} from a reduce_while. Atoms: opus-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 use one parse_code/1 clause per string; haiku-2 uses one case clause per string after trimming and upcasing; haiku-1 keeps the trimmed, upcased string and checks it against a literal list (@discount_codes), clean as in earlier grades. Money: integer div in all five; opus-1 rounds the discount to the nearest cent (155 with SAVE10 gives 638), the other four round down (639).

Naming (unchanged): domain names throughout. Bare `_` is not counted, as before: the `_ ->` clauses (sonnet-1 lines 43 and 95, sonnet-2 lines 42 and 96) and sonnet-2's function heads (line 90 `defp parse_code(_), do: :error`, line 102 `defp item_discount(_, _subtotal), do: 0`, line 105 `defp shipping_fee(_), do: @shipping_fee`), which the 2026-10-22-b and 2026-10-22-c baseline grades passed in the same functions. The stricter reading of "Give ignored values a descriptive name with a leading underscore (`_reason`, `_opts`) when it tells the reader what is being ignored." would turn sonnet-2, and Sonnet, to violated; I kept the earlier standard so the sweeps stay comparable.

Verified in scratch copies of each run's project (lib, test, mix.exs, mix.lock, .formatter.exs; deps from one mix deps.get): mix format --check-formatted, mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors (no warnings), mix credo --strict (no issues) and mix test pass in all five (opus-1 19 tests, haiku-1 17, haiku-2 15, sonnet-1 15, sonnet-2 15), matching result.json. A mix run probe with 2 x APPLE at 100 cents gives 699, 679 with SAVE10 and 200 with FREESHIP in all five, as bare integers except the Sonnet runs' {:ok, 699}, {:ok, 679}, {:ok, 200}. BOGUS returns {:error, :unknown_code} in all five. A second code is rejected by opus-1 and both Sonnet runs ({:error, :code_already_applied}) and replaces the first in both Haiku runs. " save10 " is accepted only by the Haiku runs. Removing 5 of 2 units empties the items, 1 of 2 leaves 1, and an absent SKU leaves the cart unchanged in all five. An empty cart totals 499 in all five. No lib file has String.to_atom/1, String.to_existing_atom/1 or a float.

other_violations follows the 2026-10-31 grades: Enum.reduce sums where Enum.sum_by/2 fits (haiku-1, haiku-2; opus-1 uses Enum.sum_by, and the Sonnet reduce_while halts on a missing price); two-step pipelines on one line, in lib (haiku-1 line 54, haiku-2 line 89 in a case subject) and in tests (opus-1 lines 35, 91 and 113, sonnet-1 line 65, sonnet-2 line 66); bare {:ok, cart} = arrange matches (all five) and bind-then-== (both Haiku runs) under Assert with patterns; inline case clauses past the about-70-character limit of the Inline `->` clauses rule (opus-1 line 37 at 84, haiku-1 line 38 and haiku-2 line 40 at 86). Checked and not listed: haiku-2 line 58 at 69 characters, under the limit; the inline fn bodies inside Enum.sum_by and Enum.reduce_while; the Sonnet reduce_while clauses (58 and 43 characters, both bodies a tuple), as the 2026-10-31 grades treat them; the one-expression block bodies of the second apply_code/2 clause (opus-1 lines 57-59, sonnet-2 lines 70-72), which the 2026-10-31 grades did not list; explanatory comments in the Haiku tests; the multi-line test pipelines starting with Cart.new(), which follow the project's own test file; and the project's own add_item/3 and total_quantity/1.
